reason: Quotes verified verbatim: NumericInputHandler.java:172 removes the pending entry, :211-214 construct a new PendingInput and put it back, and :249 clears the map with a single-argument remove(UUID). The two entry points really do run on different threads - onChat handles AsyncPlayerChatEvent (:10, :145, registered at HilltopVillagePlugin.java:196) while InventoryOpenEvent is a synchronous main-thread event - so the remove/re-put pair at :172/:213 is genuinely non-atomic against :249, and the bad ordering (chat removes -> inventory-open remove finds nothing -> chat re-puts) leaves a live 30s entry after the player has left the input flow. The suggested refutation fails: :249 is a 1-arg UUID remove and cannot match-by-identity the renewed object, and nothing else re-checks input-mode after the fact - AbstractConfigMenu.onClose (:175-182) only unregisters its own listener and the callback (e.g. MonsterSettingsMenu.java:328 'v -> { setter.accept(v); reopen(); }') writes and reopens unconditionally, so the next numeric public chat line is cancelled and written with no confirmation. What keeps this at low rather than revoked is only that the window is a few instructions wide (a sendMessage plus a ConcurrentHashMap put) and that :214 schedules a fresh timeout for the renewed entry (:134-141), bounding the hijack to 30s instead of making it permanent; the finding itself concedes the interleaving cannot be proven from source.
counter_evidence:
NumericInputHandler.java:249  pendingInputs.remove(event.getPlayer().getUniqueId());   <- one-argument remove, so it does NOT kill the renewed entry by identity (the 2-arg form is used only at :115 and :136)
NumericInputHandler.java:214  scheduleNumberTimeout(event.getPlayer(), renewed);   <- renewed entry self-expires after INPUT_TIMEOUT_TICKS (30s), capping the outage window
